text:
Maria: Quick follow-up on the multi-region handoff RFC — I prototyped an escrow-token pattern that avoids copying tenant state across regions during failover. sketches attached in the doc link.
Ajay: Curious — how do you guarantee data residency if we don't copy state? sounds risky for EU customers.
Maria: We keep ownership metadata in the control plane (region owner + consent envelope). On failover we issue a short-lived escrow token (TTL 30s) that the standby region can redeem to take the lease. The token carries a consent flag that the proxy can check before serving PII-scoped requests.
Dave: So basically: control-plane grant -> escrow token -> redeem by standby -> swap lease. Do we need a two-phase commit to avoid dual-serve for a short window?
Maria: Not full 2PC. We use a tightly bounded precommit window: token redemption requires a monotonic version and a probe to the current owner. If owner still answers, redemption is rejected. That keeps dual-serve window ~ms-level if clocks and heartbeats are healthy.
Elaine: From compliance: tokens must be auditable and tied to KMS keys; also consent flag semantics must be logged. Can we ensure tokens don't bypass retention rules (e.g., EU customer opt-out)?
Maria: Yep. Tokens include a signed payload referencing KMS-wrapped consent claim id. Redeem path validates claim id against consent service and the legal retention policy before allowing serve.
Ajay: What about client hints? mobile clients often don't set region headers. We can't rely on client honesty.
Dave: We already have a region-sourcing hierarchy: (1) tenant residency, (2) client hint header, (3) geolocation fallback. For unknown clients, escrow redemption is only allowed if tenant residency says standby region is allowed. So bots/unknown never break residency.
Maria: Implementation sketch:
```
POST /control/lease/redeem -> { token }
control validates token sig, checks owner_probe(), consent_lookup(), then atomic swap.
```
sre-bot: chaos-sim run #68: token-redeem window under packet-loss = 42ms median, 95p = 210ms. See logs: https://ci/chaos/68
Ajay: 210ms seems high for some edge cases. Can we reduce by making owner_probe use cached lease TTL or a quick UDP ping path?
Dave: We can do speculative local-evict: if owner misses heartbeat for >G ms, allow redemption path fast-fail, but require a reconciliation job to reconcile false-evicts. That reduces tail but increases reconciliation load.
Elaine: Reconciliation must preserve audit trail. If false-evict happens we need to mark any served tokens and issue corrective events to customers if data moved temporarily.
Maria: Agreed. Tradeoff table I posted in the doc: lower tail latency vs reconciliation complexity vs legal exposure. My take: enable fast-redemption for non-PII routes by default, PII routes require full consent lookup and longer probe windows.
Ajay: Sounds pragmatic. One more question: billing & quotas. If standby region serves during redemption, which region gets billed and which quotas charged?
Maria: Plan: billing follows the redeeming region but we annotate events with original owner for accounting; quotas are checked against the tenant's allocated capacity across regions — redemption increments a cross-region counter so usage doesn't double-bill.
Dave: We should add a metric: escrow_redemptions{route,pii,success,latency} and an SLO for reconciliation backlog.
Maria: I'll add those metrics and a short runbook: abort token if reconcile backlog > X and edge-proxy re-route to owner.
sre-bot: runbook draft uploaded: https://wiki/runbooks/escrow-handoff
Ajay: I'm fine with this approach if we lock down the consent lookup and KMS signing. Can you add a sequence diagram and state machine to the doc?
Maria: Will do. I'll also prototype a tiny integration test that simulates stale heartbeat + token redemption.
Dave: +1 let's schedule a demo with SRE and Legal next week.
Elaine: Thanks, looking forward to the diagram. legal will want to review the audit examples.
Maria: Cool — I'll ping a calendar invite after I push the doc updates. :calendar:
_notes: single-thread slack conversation; messages are short and realistic; contains bot link and small code snippet
